div.head: VIII Atr 35
div.ab: Cristenum mannum gebirað swiðe rihte, þæt he Godes abilgðe wrece swiðe georne.
Cristenum mannan gebirað swiðe rihte þæt he Godes abilgðe wrece swiðe georne.
Cristenum mannan gebirað swiðe rihte þæt he Godes abilgðe wrece swiðe georne.
Christlichem Menschen [König Cnut] geziemt sehr mit Recht, dass er Beleidigung gegen Gott sehr ernstlich bestrafe.
It very rightly befits a Christian man [king, Cnut] to avenge offences against God very zealously.
It is the duty most incumbent upon a Christian man that he should avenge offences against God with the utmost diligence.
It belongs very rightly to a Christian man to avenge very zealously offences against God.
It is most justly appropriate that a Christian should avenge affronts to God with the greatest resolve.

div.note: ‘mannum’ is wrong according to what follows; II Cn 40.2 has ‘cyninge’ (Liebermann). Liebermann compares VIII Atr 2.1.

note.seg: laut des folgenden he falsch; cyninge II Cn. 40, 2.
wrong in view of the following he; cyninge II Cn. 40, 2.

Cf. 2, 1. The reading of the MS (Cristenum mannum…he) can hardly be correct as it stands. The simplest change is to emend mannum to mannan as is done in the text on p 126. Manna is not a common word in late O.E. although the phrase þissum mannan occurs in the Blickling Homilies, 247, 18. Liebermann suggests cyninge for mannum from II Cn. 40, 2.
